title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. U_1 = U_{0,3} = P^1 - {0,1,infinity} over Q. U_n is the Fermat curve x^n + y^n = 1 with its cusps removed. It is the Galois cover of U_{0,3} with group mu_n^{{0,1,infinity}}/mu_n (diagonal), cut out by the quotient pi^_{0,3} -> pi^_{0,3}^ab / n. Here M^ = pi^_{0,3}^ab, which is the cokernel of the diagonal Z^(1) -> Z^(1)^{{0,1,infinity}}, so M^ is isomorphic to Z^(1)^2 as a Gamma_Q-module.

The extensions. E_1 is the arithmetic fundamental group of the stack [U_{0,3}/S_3] modulo the commutator subgroup of the geometric part. It is an extension 1 -> M^ -> E_1 -> Gamma_Q x S_3 -> 1. The groups E_n are the preimages of the subgroups nM^ (diagram (373) on the previous page).

This page.
- A distinguished (tangential) base point J of U_{0,3,Q} = U_{1,Q} gives a geometric point of every U_{n,Q} above J.
- It therefore gives a splitting E_1 = (Gamma_Q x S_3) semi-direct M^ (eq. 375).
- In this splitting, E_n ⊂ E_1 is the semi-direct product (Gamma_Q x S_3) semi-direct nM^, where nM^ =: M^[n] (eq. 376).
- Grothendieck remarks that these interpretations are instances of the general 'prop-flemme' of p. 711' ff.
- A rational point x_n in U_n(Q) gives, by functoriality of pi_1, a splitting of the extension E_n^! = Gamma_Q semi-direct nM^ (eq. 377). This is the part of E_n lying over Gamma_Q x {1}.

What the next page does with this.
- The M^[n]-conjugacy class of that splitting determines the class of the induced splitting of E_1, hence the point x_1 in U_1(Q).
- So it determines x_n up to gamma_n = mu_n(Q)^3/mu_n(Q). For n odd, gamma_n is trivial.
- Splitting classes form H^1(Gamma_Q, nM^), which is H^1(Gamma_Q, Z^(1)) ⊗ M, i.e. (Q^*)^ ⊗ M, i.e. G(Q)^ for a rank-2 torus G. This is the Kummer map.

Purpose. This is an anabelian, 'abelianized section conjecture' attack on rational points of Fermat curves, i.e. on Fermat's Last Theorem. One classifies the splittings of the metabelian-type extension E_n and asks which can come from rational points.
errors: E_n^! (the extension of Gamma_Q alone) should be the subgroup of E_n lying over Gamma_Q x {1}, not a quotient. 'quotient de' is either a slip or a misreading.

The page uses the S_3-symmetric splitting but does not justify that the base point J is S_3-invariant (or invariant up to conjugation). The previous page notes the canonical splittings are only unique up to S_3 x Z/2 and M^-conjugation, so the S_3-equivariance of (375) needs care.

On the next page, the step from the class in H^1(Gamma_Q, nM^) to x_1 uses injectivity of the Kummer map on U_1(Q). That holds, since x and 1-x are recovered from their Kummer classes in (Q^*)^; Q^* injects into its profinite completion because it is torsion-free mod ±1 and finitely generated locally. The argument is left implicit.

ideas.what: Tangential base point on P^1-{0,1,inf} giving a canonical splitting of the (abelianized) arithmetic fundamental group, and compatible geometric points on all Fermat covers
ideas.modern_name: tangential base points (Deligne), splitting of pi_1 of P^1-{0,1,inf}
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Galois action on pi_1 of moduli / Teichmüller tower, tangential base points implicit); Longue Marche

ideas.what: Rational points of Fermat curves give splittings of Gamma_Q semi-direct nM^. The splitting classes lie in H^1(Gamma_Q, M^) = (Q^*)^ ⊗ M, and determine the point up to mu_n(Q)^3/mu_n(Q), which is trivial for n odd
ideas.modern_name: abelian/metabelian section conjecture for Fermat curves; Kummer map on Fermat curves; Galois action on (relative) homology of Fermat curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (1986, Fermat curves and Jacobi sums via pi^_{0,3}); Anderson (1989); Ellenberg (2-nilpotent descent); Davis–Pries–Stojanoska–Wickelgren (2016–)
ideas.where_published: Not known in published texts; the Longue Marche (1981) is circulated but this continuation (pages 650 bis–787) is unpublished

ideas.what: Using the S_3-stack [U_{0,3}/S_3] so that the extensions carry the S_3 symmetry of the Fermat curve
ideas.modern_name: orbifold/stacky fundamental group of M_{0,4}/S_3 (or of the S_3-quotient)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (automorphism groups / stacks of moduli)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly sets up an anabelian (abelianized pi_1 / section-type) approach to rational points on Fermat curves. He identifies the space of candidate splittings with H^1(Gamma_Q, Z^(1)) ⊗ M = (Q^*)^ ⊗ M, and observes that for odd n a splitting determines the rational point. This anticipates the later program of Ellenberg and of Davis–Pries–Stojanoska–Wickelgren on Galois action on Fermat curve (relative) homology and obstructions to rational points.
missed.quote: Un pt x_n rationnel /Q de U_n définit un scindage de l'extension (de Γ_Q par nM^ = M^[n]) ... (377) E_n^! ≃ Γ_Q.(nM^) (½ direct)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This documents Grothendieck as having concretely pursued a section-conjecture route to FLT-type questions. This is not usually credited to him, and the unpublished pages may contain further determinations of which splitting classes can come from points.

missed.claim: The program on the next page — determining all M^[n]-conjugacy classes of splittings and deciding which can 'reasonably' come from x_n in U_n(Q) — is announced but is not completed at this abelian level. At the abelian level it cannot decide the question; higher nilpotent or metabelian quotients would be needed.
missed.quote: Ceci nous amène à déterminer toutes les classes de M^[n]-conjugaison possibles de tels scindages, afin d'examiner (si faire se peut) lesquels peuvent raisonnablement correspondre à un x_n ∈ U_n(Q)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical precursor to nonabelian Chabauty / nilpotent descent applied to Fermat curves.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on this page is the routine Kummer-theoretic setup. What is notable is that it shows Grothendieck explicitly attacking rational points of Fermat curves via splittings of abelianized arithmetic fundamental groups. That is a section-conjecture approach to Fermat not attested in his published texts, and it anticipates later work (Ihara, Anderson, Ellenberg, DPSW).
